parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
For my presentation, I’m going to talk to you about the archaeological dig I went on in the summer at the site of Trimerra in southern Europe near the Mediterranean Sea. The site is backed by a range of mountains to the north, overlooking a green, fertile plain to the south.

Let me first give you an idea of the history of the area and the growth of the city. The first evidence we have of human settlement in the Trimerra area is of hunter-gatherers around 12,000 years ago. Later, about 5,000 years ago, farmers settled along the many rivers which cut across the plain, and later still, from about 2,500 years ago, the city of Trimerra was established, and it soon became a regional centre for trade. The city was first invaded by the Greeks around 300 B.C., then the Romans in 100 B.C. Under the Romans, it became very prosperous and traded in grain, olives, and pottery. Then, in 518 A.D., an earthquake destroyed Trimerra, and the city was abandoned.

However, much of the city was covered with soil and rock by the earthquake, and so, luckily for us archaeologists, many of the ruins survived intact. The first report on the ruins dates back to around 1706, when a French explorer passed through the area. He thought that what he was seeing were the ruins of a castle.

In the 19th century, a British archaeologist began to explore the site, and later, a Polish count made the first map of the area and recorded some of the inscriptions which were visible on the surface. However, it was not until 1982 that a Swedish archaeologist made a full survey of the ruins of Trimerra.

The first remains to be excavated were identified as those of the market. Archaeologists were trying to establish how trade was organised here and the type of goods which were commonly bought and sold.

In and around this area, various examples of silver coins have come to light. During the Roman period, it appears that the city was completely reorganised. The public squares were paved, as were the main streets.

There is also some proof to suggest that textile production was an important industry. The huge prosperity during this period was helped by the fact that the city was responsible for provisioning the Roman army in the eastern region.

Now what I’d like to do is talk about some of the more important buildings in some detail.

First of all, the Doric House. This Greek building is located to the east of the city, near the copper mines. This building is where the local population would come to get their water. The fact that the ruins were so well preserved has meant that the team of archaeologists excavating the site has been able to partially reconstruct the building.

The remains of a theatre are to be found in the northwest of the city, adjacent to the river, where a magnificent bridge made of stone has recently been unearthed. In Roman times, the theatre appears to have been extended and may have been able to take up to 5,000 spectators.

In the southwestern corner of the city are the remains of an elegant stairway. It dates back to about 37 AD. The stairway is decorated with sculptures of lions, as opposed to bears, found in other parts of the site. This is possibly because of trading links with Africa.

Finally, the most recent discovery has been at the site of the Roman baths, in the central area of Trimera. Here, a huge statue of an emperor from the Roman period was excavated.

It appears to have been carved in pieces and then taken to the site and put together. The statue is very finely detailed, and the recent discovery of marble toes and the hem of a dress suggests that a companion statue may also be buried in the bath’s site. analyses.content: 录音在列举罗马时期贸易产品时，明确提到了谷物、橄榄和陶器。
Under the Romans, it became very prosperous and traded in grain, olives, and pottery.
你可能会根据常识想填入其他农产品，但必须严格听取录音中并列出现的最后一个词。
The first report on the ruins dates back to around 1706, when a French explorer passed through the area. He thought that what he was seeing were the ruins of a castle.
注意时间点1706年的定位，不要把后文19世纪出现的地图或铭文信息填入此处。
法国探险家在1706年经过此处时，主观认为看到的废墟是一座城堡。
However, it was not until 1982 that a Swedish archaeologist made a full survey of the ruins of Trimerra.
你可能想填入map，但map是此前波兰伯爵做的工作，1982年对应的是“full survey”。
直到1982年，瑞典考古学家才对这片遗址进行了全面的勘测。

The first remains to be excavated were identified as those of the market. Archaeologists were trying to establish how trade was organised here and the type of goods which were commonly bought and sold.
不要被后文提到的具体商品干扰，题目要求填的是第一个被挖掘的“地点”。
录音直接指出第一批被挖掘出来的遗骸被确认为市场所在地。
In and around this area, various examples of silver coins have come to light.
你可能只填了coins，虽然语义对但漏掉了限定词silver，或者误填了前文提到的grain等贸易品。
在市场区域及其周边，考古人员发现了各种银币的样本。
证据显示纺织生产在当时是一个非常重要的行业。
There is also some proof to suggest that textile production was an important industry.
注意industry（行业）这个提示词，录音中在important industry之前出现的修饰词就是答案。

analyses.content: First of all, the Doric House. This Greek building is located to the east of the city, near the copper mines. This building is where the local population would come to get their water.
你可能会被前面的copper mines（铜矿）干扰，但那是地理位置参考，居民来这里的真实目的是为了water。
当地居民来到这座希腊风格的建筑（Doric House）是为了取水。
The remains of a theatre are to be found in the northwest of the city, adjacent to the river, where a magnificent bridge made of stone has recently been unearthed.
题目表格中已有stone一词，你只需要填入名词bridge，不要重复填写stone。
剧院位于河流旁边，而河上最近出土了一座宏伟的石桥。
The stairway is decorated with sculptures of lions, as opposed to bears, found in other parts of the site.
录音中提到了bears（熊）作为对比项，那是其他地方发现的，你要听清as opposed to（而不是）后面的排除信息。
这座优雅的楼梯上装饰着狮子的雕塑。
Finally, the most recent discovery has been at the site of the Roman baths, in the central area of Trimera. Here, a huge statue of an emperor from the Roman period was excavated.
你可能想填statue，但表格中已经给出“A statue of a...”，此处需要填的是雕像的人物身份。
在罗马浴场中心区域的遗址中，挖掘出了一尊巨大的罗马皇帝雕像。
